distractors.reason: 'Highly' is used with adjectives of quality or value (highly recommended, highly skilled), not with 'aware'. We say 'fully aware'.
'Deeply' is used with feelings and emotions (deeply moved, deeply concerned), not with 'aware'.
'Greatly' is used for amounts and changes (greatly improved). It is not normally placed before 'aware'.

example_sentence: Although she was ___ aware of the risks, she decided to continue.
l1_interference: Falantes de português costumam traduzir 'altamente ciente' ou 'muito ciente' por 'highly aware' ou 'very aware', por influência de 'altamente' e 'muito'. Em inglês, usa-se 'fully aware' para expressar 'totalmente ciente'.
explanation: In English, 'fully' is the natural degree adverb before 'aware', meaning completely conscious of something. 'Highly' and 'deeply' are used with other kinds of adjectives and verbs, so learn 'fully aware' as one unit.

related_collocations.example: Please make sure you are fully informed before you sign the contract.
The company hired a highly skilled engineer.
Many residents were strongly opposed to the new road.

memory_tip: FULLY = completely (fully aware, fully informed) | HIGHLY = to a high level of quality (highly skilled, highly recommended)
